verses.84:2: {bened}, Senhor, a vossa terra: * {av2} o cativeiro de Jacó.
verses.84:3: Perdoastes a iniquidade do vosso povo: * cobristes todos os seus pecados.
verses.84:4: {mitig} toda a vossa ira: * {av4} da ira da vossa indignação.
verses.84:5: {conv}, Deus, {salut}: * e {av5} de nós a vossa ira.
verses.84:6: Acaso {irasc} conosco para sempre? * ou estendereis a vossa ira de geração em geração?
verses.84:7: Deus, voltando-vos, {vivif}: * e o vosso povo se alegrará em vós.
verses.84:8: Mostrai-nos, Senhor, a vossa misericórdia: * e dai-nos a vossa salvação.
verses.84:9: Ouvirei o que o Senhor Deus {loq} em mim: * porque ele {pax9}.
verses.84:10: {verum}, perto dos que o temem está a sua salvação: * para que habite a glória na nossa terra.
verses.84:11: A misericórdia e a verdade se encontraram: * a justiça e a paz {oscul}.
verses.84:12: A verdade {orta} da terra: * e a justiça olhou do céu.
verses.84:13: Pois o Senhor dará {benign}: * e a nossa terra dará o seu fruto.
verses.84:14: A justiça andará diante dele: * e porá no caminho os seus passos.

decisions.why: God blessing a thing. The row *benedícere* (God → man) is *bendizer*, open (D11), and it has been used where God blesses: 5:12b *bendireis ao justo*, 28:11 *bendirá o seu povo*, 64:12 *Bendireis a coroa do ano*, 66:2 *nos bendiga*. The Greek here is εὐδόκησας ('you were pleased with'), but the Latin says *bless* and is followed. This line is the Introit of Advent III (and the Mass of Advent I, Adv3-5 — grep), so it will be said and sung alone; every Portuguese parallel has *abençoar*.

options.label: Bendissestes
options.note: Ruling: the row, as 64:12, 28:11 — one verb for blessing in the psalter while D11 is open.

options.label: Abençoastes
options.note: MS1932 *Abençoaste*; the common verb for God blessing; one syllable lighter in the ear.

decisions.latin: avertísti captivitátem … avertísti ab ira … avérte iram tuam
decisions.why: *Avértere* three times in four verses: the psalm turns on it (and on *convértere*, 84:5, 84:7). The row *avértere* names 84:2 for *afastar o cativeiro* (as 13:7) and keeps *desviar* for anger (77:38b *desviou a sua ira*). Taking the row literally would split the psalm's one verb into two within four verses. Ruled: *afastar* all three times, so the repetition the Latin has is heard (rule 6). 84:4 has no object in Latin or Greek (ἀπέστρεψας ἀπό, DRB 'thou hast turned away from'), so the verb is reflexive — *vos afastastes da ira*; MS1932's *suspendeste o furor* supplies another verb and object. 84:5 is the second half of the Compline versicle (*R. Et avérte iram tuam a nobis* → *E afastai de nós a vossa ira*), and MS1932 has *afasta de nós a tua ira* there. Cost: 84:5 and 77:38b render *avértere iram* with two verbs.

options.label: afastar ×3
options.note: Ruling: one verb for the psalm's one verb; the row's 84:2 wording.

options.label: afastar / desviar
options.note: the row as written: *desviar* with anger, as 77:38b; splits the repetition.

decisions.why: L&S: to make mild or soft; of anger, to soothe, assuage (*iras*, Ovid). *Abrandar* is the verb's own image (*mitis* → *brando*) and the plainer word; the cognate *mitigar* is understood but formal (MS1932, DRB 'mitigated'). The Greek κατέπαυσας ('made cease') is not followed. Not in the glossary; proposed as a row.

options.label: Abrandastes
options.note: Ruling: the image of softening, plain.

options.label: Mitigastes
options.note: MS1932, DRB; the cognate.

options.label: Aplacastes
options.note: appease; L&S gives the sense, but it is *placáre*'s word.

decisions.why: The same imperative as Ps 79's refrain (*Deus, convérte nos*, 79:4, 8, 20), which the Ps 79 agent ruled *convertei-nos* under D25's exception as extended at 18:8 and 22:2 (God turning souls), and which asked that 84:5 follow it; the formula row for 79:4 names 84:5. Followed: ἐπίστρεψον ἡμᾶς holds both 'bring us back' and 'turn us to you', and *convertei-nos* holds both, the religious sense first — how this line is prayed at Compline (Common/Prayers.txt: *V. Convérte nos, Deus, salutáris noster. R. Et avérte iram tuam a nobis*) and in the Lenten collect (Quad1-1). DRB 'Convert us'; MS1932 *Converte-nos*. Cost: 84:7 *convérsus* (God turning) is *voltando-vos*, so one root becomes two verbs two verses apart, as in Ps 79 (79:15).

options.label: Convertei-nos
options.note: Ruling: Ps 79's formula; D25; DRB, MS1932.

options.label: Fazei-nos voltar
options.note: the *convértere* row's verb, causative (52:7); keeps the echo with 84:7 *voltando-vos*; heavier; Ps 79's option 1.

decisions.why: The row *salutáris* (of God, in apposition) → *Salvador*, applied at 64:6 *Escutai-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador* and 78:9 *Deus, nosso Salvador*; this is the third of the three places the row named. The Greek here is τῶν σωτηρίων ἡμῶν ('God of our salvations'), but the Latin makes it a title, and the Latin is followed; DRB 'O God our saviour', MS1932 *ó Deus, salvador nosso*. Kept apart from 84:8, 84:10 *salutáre* → *salvação* (D6).

options.label: nosso Salvador
options.note: Ruling: the row, as 64:6, 78:9.

options.label: nossa salvação
options.note: closer to the Greek's σωτηρίων and echoes 84:8, 84:10; but *salutáris* is masculine, a person.

decisions.why: The row is *irar-se*. The future *vos irareis* is a knot of r's (the Ps 79 stylist on 79:5 *quoúsque irascéris*), and Ps 79 took *estareis irado* — the root kept, the future said with a copula, which D2 allows. Same here, for the same Latin form. *nobis* → *conosco*.

options.label: estareis irado
options.note: Ruling: as 79:5; MS1932 *estarás … irado*.

options.label: vos irareis
options.note: the row's verb, one word for one.

decisions.why: *vivificáre → vivificar* (row; 118, 40:3, 70:20 *voltando-vos, me vivificastes*, 79:19 *vós nos vivificareis*). The Latin's emphatic *tu* is kept as *vós*, placed after the participle so that neither *vós, voltando-vos* stammers nor the clause opens on a clitic. The blind readers have not known *vivificar* several times; the row keeps it.

options.label: vós nos vivificareis
options.note: Ruling: the row; = 79:19.

options.label: vós nos dareis a vida
options.note: MS1932 *restituir-nos-ás a vida*; the row's option.

decisions.latin: quid loquátur in me Dóminus Deus
decisions.why: *loquátur* is a present subjunctive in an indirect question (the Greek has a future, λαλήσει); the same verb returns at once as *loquétur pacem*, so *falar* both times keeps the Latin's repetition. *in me → em mim*, not MS1932's *me disser*: the Latin places the speaking inside the psalmist. The Latin's order (*o que fala em mim o Senhor Deus*) was weighed and refused: *o que fala* can be heard as 'the one who speaks'.

options.label: fala
options.note: Ruling: present, as the Latin's tense.

options.label: dirá
options.note: the Greek's future; another verb, loses the repetition.

decisions.latin: quóniam loquétur pacem in plebem suam. Et super sanctos suos: et in eos …
decisions.why: *loquétur pacem* is the accusative of content, as *loqui mendácium → falar mentira* (row; 16:9b *falou soberba*), so *falará paz*: God speaks peace, he does not talk about it (*falar de paz*) or announce it (*anunciar*, MS1932, which is another verb). The Latin varies its prepositions (*in … super … in*) where the Greek has ἐπί three times; kept as *para … sobre … para* — each is natural Portuguese, and *sobre os seus santos* keeps the picture of a word spoken over them. Subject *ele* supplied.

options.label: falará paz para … sobre … para

forms.pax9: falará paz para o seu povo

options.note: Ruling: the Latin's verb, object and prepositions.

options.label: falará de paz ao … aos … aos

forms.pax9: falará de paz ao seu povo

options.note: the Greek's one preposition, and *falar de*, the common build; *de paz* can be heard as 'about peace'.

options.label: anunciará a paz ao … aos … aos

forms.pax9: anunciará a paz ao seu povo

options.note: MS1932, DM1962 (from the Hebrew); another verb.

decisions.why: The Latin *ad cor* ('to the heart') is the Latin's own; the Greek has 'those who turn their heart to him', the Hebrew something else again. It can be heard as turning back into oneself (*redíte ad cor*, Is 46:8) or turning with the whole heart — the ambiguity is kept. The verb: men turning, and conversion the sense (DRB 'converted', MS1932 *se convertem*), so D25's exception, *converter*. MS1932's *de coração* ('sincerely') resolves the phrase and is refused as a ruling.

options.label: convertem ao coração
options.note: Ruling: the Latin's words; D25; DRB 'converted to the heart'.

options.label: voltam para o coração
options.note: the *convértere* row's default verb.

options.label: convertem de coração
options.note: MS1932; the easier idiom, but it says 'sincerely', which the Latin does not.

decisions.why: The row is *todavia* (applied in Pss 31, 38, 48, 61, 72, 74). Here there is no contrast to answer: the Greek πλήν is asseverative, and DRB has 'Surely', MS1932 *Sim*. The row is followed; *Na verdade* (Ps 38's option) is kept as the option, for this verse especially.

options.label: Todavia
options.note: Ruling: the row.

options.label: Na verdade
options.note: the asseverative sense (DRB 'Surely'); Ps 38's option; collides with *véritas → verdade* in 84:11–12.

decisions.why: The plain word for the image: *se beijaram* (DRB 'have kissed'). MS1932's *se oscularam* is the cognate, a bookish word in Brazil now. The verse is famous as it stands; the image is kept concrete (rule 5).

options.label: se beijaram
options.note: Ruling: plain and concrete.

options.label: se oscularam
options.note: MS1932, DM1962; the cognate.

decisions.why: *oríri → nascer* (row; 71:7 *Nascerá nos seus dias a justiça*). ἀνέτειλεν is used of a star rising and a plant springing. The Christmas office sets this verse as an antiphon (Sancti/12-25, *Véritas de terra * orta est*) and the Fathers read the birth in it; *nasceu* carries both the birth and the springing. MS1932 and DM1962 *brotou* choose the plant only.

options.label: nasceu
options.note: Ruling: the row, as 71:7.

options.label: brotou
options.note: MS1932, DM1962: the plant image alone.

decisions.why: *benígnitas → benignidade* (settled, D44; the row names 84:13). The Latin has no possessive; the article is what Portuguese needs before an abstract object. MS1932 adds *a sua*. The blind readers have not known *benignidade* twice; *bondade* stays the option (it is *bónitas*'s word).

options.label: a benignidade
options.note: Ruling: D44, nothing added.

options.label: a sua benignidade
options.note: MS1932 *a sua bondade*; supplies a possessive.

options.label: a bondade
options.note: the row's option; *bónitas*'s word.

choices.84:2: Introit of Advent III; each colon reads alone. *captívitas → cativeiro*, *Jacob → Jacó* (13:7).
choices.84:3: *remíttere → perdoar* (row, 31:5b); *opérire → cobrir* (the *tégere* row names this verse, 31:1). *plebs → povo* (row). *eórum → os seus*: after *vosso povo* the possessive can only be theirs.
choices.84:4: *ira … ira* is the Latin's repetition, kept. *indignátio → indignação* (row).
choices.84:5: The Compline versicle: *V. Convertei-nos, Deus, nosso Salvador. R. E afastai de nós a vossa ira.* Natural order in the second colon (*de nós* before the object).
choices.84:6: *numquid → acaso* (row). *a generatióne in generatiónem → de geração em geração*, as 76:9 and the formula row.
choices.84:7: *convérsus* of God → *voltando-vos*, as 70:20 (*voltando-vos, me vivificastes*). *lætári → alegrar-se* (row).
choices.84:8: The Preces and Advent versicle, which must stand alone as V and R: *V. Mostrai-nos, Senhor, a vossa misericórdia. R. E dai-nos a vossa salvação.* *salutáre tuum → a vossa salvação*, = the Nunc dimittis (D6). Natural order (*dai-nos* before the object). *Mostrai* and *dai* are safe under rule 3 (past *mostrei*, *dei*). The glossary had no formula row for it; one is proposed.
choices.84:9: *audíre → ouvir* (not an imperative, D3 allows it).
choices.84:10: The copula *está* supplied (D2). *timéntes eum → os que o temem* (33:8). *ut inhábitet → para que habite*, the purpose clause kept (22:6b row); MS1932 turns it into a statement.
choices.84:11: *obviáre sibi → encontrar-se* (L&S cites this verse: 'to meet'); *uma com a outra* not added — *se encontraram* is already reciprocal. Soft check: rhyme *encontraram / beijaram* accepted — the Latin sets two perfects at the two cadences (*obviavérunt / osculátæ sunt*), and every Portuguese perfect plural ends in *-aram* (the option *oscularam* too); reordering to avoid it would be inversion for its own sake.
choices.84:12: *prospícere → olhar* (row, which names this verse; 13:2 *olhou do céu*). The Christmas antiphon is the first colon.
choices.84:13: *étenim → pois* (row). *dabit … dabit* kept as *dará … dará* (MS1932 varies the second, *produzirá*); 66:6 *a terra deu o seu fruto*. The Advent versicle (*V. Dóminus dabit benignitátem, et terra nostra dabit fructum suum*) is this verse without *Étenim*.
choices.84:14: *ambuláre → andar* (row); *gressus → passos* (16:5). *os seus passos* keeps the Latin's open reference (justice's own steps or the Lord's: *suos* against the Greek αὐτοῦ).

audit.note: Psalm-level draft from consult/parallels/ps084.md (with the Diurnal Monástico 1962). Hard readings: 84:4 *avertísti ab ira* with no object (reflexive); 84:9 *loquátur in me* and *loquétur pacem in plebem … super … in*; 84:9b *convertúntur ad cor*; 84:10 *Verúmtamen* without contrast; 84:14 *suos*. Liturgical texts that read alone: 84:2 (Introit, Advent III), 84:5 (Compline versicle), 84:8 (Preces / Advent versicle), 84:12a (Christmas antiphon), 84:13 (Advent versicle). The glossary had no formula row for 84:8; the Ps 79 refrain row fixes *Convérte nos* (followed, at the Ps 79 agent's request).

Hard pass. Soft, all accepted: 84:3b -4 (*cobristes todos os seus pecados* is complete; nothing to add); 84:6a +4 (*estareis irado*, the copula future — option *vos irareis* is 3 shorter) and 84:6b -4 (the formula *de geração em geração*); 84:7b +3 (*e o vosso povo* — article and possessive); 84:8a -3 (Portuguese *misericórdia* carries the colon); 84:9b second colon +3 (*ao coração*, the Latin's words); 84:11 rhyme accepted (see choices).
